title: Factual responsibility, verification, and sanctions
summary: Certification and verification requirements attach responsibility to statements submitted to the court. Sanctions can enforce that responsibility but require the applicable substantive standard and procedural protections.
notes: Losing a claim does not itself prove sanctionable conduct. A genuine investigation and reasonable reliance matter, and the safeguards in Hadges remain separate from the underlying merits.

sections.Meaning: Certification and verification requirements attach responsibility to statements submitted to the court. Sanctions can enforce that responsibility but require the applicable substantive standard and procedural protections.
sections.How to work through the question: Distinguish derivative-action verification in Surowitz from Rule 11 certification and the court’s other sanctions authority. Identify the document, factual or legal inquiry, alleged misconduct, notice, and procedure for imposing a sanction.
